call.title: Lesson — adding fractions
call.content:
Lesson — adding fractions

Yesterday: 3 of 3 right on equivalent fractions — on to the next topic.

## Explanation
To add fractions, the bottom numbers must match. If they do not, find a number both bottoms divide into, rewrite each fraction over it, then add the top numbers.

## Worked example
1/3 + 1/4: both 3 and 4 divide 12. 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12. 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12.

## Quiz
1. 1/2 + 1/3
2. 2/5 + 1/10
3. Write 2/4 in its simplest form. (equivalent fractions)

## Answers (no peeking)
1. 5/6  2. 1/2  3. 1/2

call.title: Lesson — equivalent fractions, again
call.content:
Lesson — equivalent fractions, again

Yesterday: 1 of 3 right (2 and 3 were upside down) — the same topic again, another way.

## Explanation
Think of a pizza. Cutting each slice in two doubles the slices but not the pizza: 1/2 is the same as 2/4. Multiply or divide top and bottom by the same number.

## Worked example
Is 3/6 the same as 1/2? Divide top and bottom by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1, 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Yes.

## Quiz
1. Write 4/8 more simply.
2. Is 2/6 the same as 1/3?
3. Fill in: 1/4 = ?/8

## Answers (no peeking)
1. 1/2  2. yes  3. 2

## Quiz
